prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup. Edit the attached AgentHarbor desktop chat application design into a substantially SIMPLER complete desktop meeting workspace. This is a layout and information-hierarchy simplification of the existing product, not a new brand or new functionality. Render one complete full-window desktop application at 1536x1024, same landscape dimensions, no browser frame. The user found the previous interface cluttered. Keep assistant conversation primary, tasks/results at the side, but eliminate duplicated information, colorful panels, repeated statuses and excessive navigation.

EXACT LAYOUT: a compact SINGLE Windows desktop title bar, with AgentHarbor left, small clear “设计预览 · 示例数据” label, and Windows minimize/maximize/close controls right. No Mac traffic lights. Below it THREE panes only: a 220px pale blue-gray sidebar, an expansive white center conversation taking most of the width, and a 280px white task inspector right. Fine 1px pane dividers. No extra icon rail, no menu row, no status footer, no fourth column. No decorative logo area. This must look like an excellent desktop messaging application, with stable panes and an anchored input area, not an admin website.

LEFT SIDEBAR: small project selector “AgentHarbor 项目” near top, a modest “新建会议” button with a plus icon, a quiet “最近会议” label, just THREE meeting rows: selected “登录重试修复”, “优化任务恢复”, “新增助手接入”. Selected row uses very pale blue fill, blue text and a small amber status dot. No dates, badges, avatar clusters, project tree or task counts in this list. Bottom has only “助手管理” and “设置” as quiet icon-and-text links. Sidebar is pale, not saturated dark blue.

CENTER: compact conversation header “登录重试修复” at 20px, and a small clickable “3 位助手” member control on the right. Do NOT repeat task status or role cards across this header. Spacious plain conversation thread with small consistent circular initial avatars in subdued blue-gray and readable author labels; no enormous bubbles, no nested cards, no thick borders. Four short messages, generously separated:
主持人  “先修复登录过期后的重试问题，验证后由 Claude Code 审核。”
Codex · 执行  “刷新逻辑已修复，现有 8 项回归测试通过。”
Under Codex's message show only two small inline links “查看改动” and “查看测试”, not large result cards.
Claude Code · 审核  “还缺少并发重试用例，暂不通过。”
主持人  “已交回 Codex 补测，完成后自动再次审核。”
The thread can have breathing room below; do not invent more UI to fill space. Only the latest host handoff has a tiny inline activity indicator “Codex 正在补充测试…”.
At the bottom of the center is a FIXED clean message composer, 100px high, fine neutral outline, placeholder “描述目标，或 @助手加入讨论…”, one attachment icon at left, one blue “发送” button at right. No recipient dropdown, no extra task chip row, no input helper toolbar, no duplicate automatic-run switch here.

RIGHT INSPECTOR: small heading “当前任务”, one compact amber text status “补测中”, then task title “补充并发重试用例”. A single muted line “执行：Codex”. Under “下一步” one concise line “重新测试，再交由 Claude Code 审核”. Under “待解决” a very restrained pale amber callout with just “并发重试尚未验证”. Below use THREE collapsed standard disclosure rows with chevrons: “验收标准”, “改动与测试”, “执行历史”. No visible checkbox list, no duplicate test counts or patch filenames, no separate large result cards, no role/member list, no timeline. A single quiet outlined “暂停任务” control near the inspector bottom. Do NOT add restart/manual-review buttons or extra primary CTAs. This side pane answers ONLY: current task, who acts next, why not complete.

VISUALS: one workhorse sans-serif family suitable for Chinese (Segoe UI / Microsoft YaHei-like), body near 16px at 1440-wide screen, dark ink readable text, only 3-4 type sizes, generous 24-32px spacing around messages. White and cool pale slate surfaces; blue only for selection, links and Send; amber only for the one incomplete-task indicator. No gradients, no shadows, no decorative textures, no multicolored participant badges, no dashboard card grid, no marketing copy. Preserve familiar desktop controls. The illustrative task is unfinished, never show final success or pretend these are actual execution records. The intended visible hierarchy is: conversation first, next action second, everything else available on demand.
userFeedback: The previous desktop meeting proposals felt cluttered. Reduce visible choices and repeated information; retain the conversation-first desktop interaction.
